title: Polynomial base-change comma equivalence with its evaluation augmentation
statement:
Let $A\to B\to C$ be maps of commutative rings. Use a common infinite cardinal bound for all rings and variable sets and small models [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E_C$ be the opposite category of pairs $(P\to B,Q\to C)$, with $P$ polynomial over $A$, $Q$ polynomial over $P$, and compatible augmentations; morphisms before taking opposites are commuting pairs of $A$-algebra maps preserving the augmentations. Let $\mathcal D_C$ be the opposite category of polynomial $B$-algebras augmented to $C$, and put $u(P,Q)=(Q\otimes_P B\to C)$. Fix $V=(H\xrightarrow{\delta}C)\in\mathcal D_C$, so $H$ is polynomial over $B$. Let $\mathcal E_H$ be the same pair category with target $H$ in place of $C$, and $\mathcal D_H$ the opposite category of polynomial $B$-algebras augmented to $H$. Write $v:\mathcal E_H\to\mathcal D_H$ for $(P,Q)\mapsto(Q\otimes_P B\to H)$ and $j:\mathcal D_H\to\mathcal D_C$ for composition of augmentation with $\delta$. All these categories have the identity-cover topology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].
There is an equivalence $e_V:(V\downarrow u)\simeq\mathcal E_H$ sending an object $((P,Q),a)$, where $a$ corresponds to $\alpha:Q\otimes_P B\to H$, to $(P\to B,Q\xrightarrow{\gamma}H)$ with $\gamma(q)=\alpha(q\otimes1)$. Its inverse uses $\alpha(q\otimes b)=\gamma(q)b$ and the augmentation $Q\to H\xrightarrow{\delta}C$. On morphisms it preserves the underlying compatible pair of algebra maps. For every commutative ring $R$ and module presheaf $K$ on $\mathcal D_C$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $G=j^{-1}K$ and $F_V((P,Q),a)=K(u(P,Q))$. This equivalence identifies $F_V$ with $e_V^{-1}v^{-1}G$ and induces a natural isomorphism
$$L\pi_{(V\downarrow u),!}^R F_V\xrightarrow{\sim}L\pi_{\mathcal E_H,!}^R(v^{-1}G)$$
in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where derived colimits and reindexing maps use [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. Under this isomorphism the bar augmentation $((U,a),x)\mapsto K(a)x$ to $K(V)[0]$ is the polynomial-target augmentation to $G(H\xrightarrow{1}H)[0]$ specified in [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek-polynomial-top]. In particular this specified augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, naturally in $K$. No polynomiality of $C$ over $B$, and no flatness of either given ring map, is assumed.

proof.text: Put $T_U=Q\otimes_P B$, with its induced augmentation $\epsilon_U:T_U\to C$. A comma object is precisely $U=(P,Q)$ together with a $B$-algebra map $\alpha:T_U\to H$ satisfying $\delta\alpha=\epsilon_U$. Apply the tensor-pushout universal property over $P$ to $Q\to H$ and the structural map $B\to H$. It gives a bijection between these $\alpha$ and compatible maps $\gamma:Q\to H$, by $\gamma(q)=\alpha(q\otimes1)$ and $\alpha(q\otimes b)=\gamma(q)b$. Restriction to $q\otimes1$ shows that the comma equation is equivalent to $\delta\gamma$ being the given augmentation of $Q$. Conversely equality on both tensor factors proves the comma equation. Thus the proposed object maps are well-defined; they change no polynomial algebra or variable set.

Let a morphism $U\to U'$ in the opposite pair category be represented by $(p:P'\to P,q:Q'\to Q)$. Its base change is $h:T_{U'}\to T_U$, $q'\otimes b\mapsto q(q')\otimes b$. The comma condition is $\alpha' =\alpha h$; by restriction to $q'\otimes1$ and uniqueness in the tensor universal property it is equivalent to $\gamma'=\gamma q$. This is exactly the morphism condition in $\mathcal E_H$. Preserve $(p,q)$ in both directions. Identities and composition are preserved since the underlying pairs are unchanged. The two object constructions are inverse by the two formulas of step 1 and tensor uniqueness, and their morphism constructions are inverse. They give $e_V$ and its inverse $r_V$. Use the same bounded models throughout; passing to skeletons instead gives the corresponding unit and counit isomorphisms.

Write $p_V:(V\downarrow u)\to\mathcal E_C$ for the projection. The functors $jve_V$ and $up_V$ have the same algebra $T_U$, augmentation $\delta\alpha=\epsilon_U$, and base-change maps. Consequently their precompositions with $K$ agree on objects and restriction maps: $e_V^{-1}v^{-1}G=F_V$. This coefficient identification is the identity on each $K(uU)$, and hence commutes with every morphism of module presheaves $K\to K'$.

Apply the derived-colimit bar theorem to $e_V$ and this coefficient identification. Its canonical map sends $(Z_n\to\cdots\to Z_0,x)$ to $(e_VZ_n\to\cdots\to e_VZ_0,x)$. The face formulas show this is a chain map. Reindexing by $r_V$ gives its inverse: in the common explicit models the composites are identity, and on small skeletons the unit and counit give equality of the derived composite maps by the theorem's natural-transformation clause. This proves the stated isomorphism in $D(R)$, with its specified direction and naturality in $K$. All indexing categories are small by the common bound.

For $W=e_VZ$ with $Z=(U,a)$, let $b_W:(H\xrightarrow{1}H)\to vW$ be the arrow of $\mathcal D_H$ opposite to $\alpha:T_U\to H$. Its image $j(b_W)$ is exactly $a:V\to uU$. The polynomial-target augmentation is, by its cited statement, reindexing along $v$ followed by the augmentation induced by the $b_W$. The bar formula therefore sends a degree-zero generator $(Z,x)$ first to $(W,x)$ and then to $G(b_W)x=K(a)x$. In negative degrees both augmentations to the degree-zero complex are zero. Thus these are the same chain map, not merely maps inducing the same degree-zero homology map; the face formula for a one-arrow chain also verifies the augmentation relation by functoriality.

Write $H=B[E]$. Apply the polynomial-top theorem with the ring map $A\to B$, target $H$, coefficient ring $R$, and presheaf $G=j^{-1}K$. Its pair category is exactly $\mathcal E_H$ and its target category is $\mathcal D_H$. The bound contains $E$ and all the rings; the topology is the identity-cover topology as required. That theorem makes its specified augmentation an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Composing with step 4 and using step 5 makes the specified comma augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. The generator formulas commute with every natural map $K\to K'$, proving naturality. Polynomiality is used only for $H$; neither the equivalence nor this application requires $C$ polynomial or either ring map flat.

Source: Stacks 08QW case i=3 (cotangent.tex ~1290-1365) prints C_{Qbar/C}, but the sheaf lives on polynomial B-algebras augmented to Qbar, so the item is right to use D_H = C_{H/B}. 08QV is then applied to H. Step 1: the tensor-pushout Mathlib leaf (clauses 2-3) gives alpha <-> gamma. I checked that gamma is compatible with P->B->H and that delta*alpha = eps_U holds because delta is B-linear. Step 2: u(f)a = a' in D_C is the same as alpha' = alpha h (variance checked), which is the same as gamma' = gamma q by uniqueness. So e_V is an isomorphism of categories on fixed models. Step 3: j v e_V(U,a) = (T_U, delta alpha) = u p_V(U,a), with the same base-change maps, so F_V = e_V^{-1} v^{-1} G on the nose. Step 4: the identity and composition clauses of derived-colimit-bar, with r_V, give the isomorphism in D(R). Its natural-transformation clause covers the skeleton variant. Step 5: polynomial-top's statement fixes its augmentation as reindexing along v followed by G(b). Here b_W is opposite to alpha and j(b_W) = a, so G(b_W) = K(a), and the two augmentations agree degree by degree; I also checked that the augmentation is a chain map on 1-chains. Step 6: polynomial-top is applied with C := H = B[E] and F := G; its categories and its v match E_H and D_H. Edge cases: E empty, B = 0, non-flat A->B, non-polynomial C and zero K are all fine. The dependency closure (330 nodes) has no cycle. Both cited nodes are in unit sk-i-curve-zero and are split and reviewed; the tensor node is a Mathlib leaf, so no tool_uses are needed. An rg -L search for the comma equivalence found no duplicate. No SGA source is used. No fixes.
